cases.title: Apple FY2024: one-time tax charge and profit-quality questions
questions: How should an analyst separate recurring profitability from a one-time tax item?
Which additional segment, product, buyback, cash-flow and accounting-note evidence is required before valuing the company?
Can net income be compared across years without adjusting for the one-time item?
cases.source_note: Official Apple FY2024 consolidated financial statements and newsroom release. Derived metrics are FinPilot calculations from the displayed official amounts.
cases.caveat: This is a financial-statement case, not a complete equity research snapshot; no price, shares, segment forecast or valuation is embedded.

cases.title: Microsoft FY2024: growth and operating leverage
questions: How much of operating-margin improvement is recurring versus mix, cloud scale or accounting presentation?
What additional segment revenue, operating income, capex and cash-flow data is needed for a research view?
How should a high operating margin be interpreted alongside growth investment and competition?
cases.source_note: Official Microsoft FY2024 income statement and annual-report entry points. Derived operating margin is revenue divided by operating income.
cases.caveat: This is not a complete stock screen or valuation; it deliberately omits price, EPS, shares and future estimates.

cases.title: NVIDIA FY2024: exceptional growth, margin and concentration questions
questions: How should an analyst test whether exceptional growth and margins can persist?
What customer, product, geography, supply-chain and capex concentration checks are required?
How sensitive is a valuation to a normalization of growth and margins?
cases.source_note: Official NVIDIA fiscal 2024 GAAP figures. Derived margins are FinPilot calculations from the displayed official amounts.
cases.caveat: The case is designed to prompt diligence, not to imply a buy/sell conclusion or future growth rate.

cases.title: WTI April 2020: negative futures price and contract mechanics
cases.instrument: WTI crude oil futures, May 2020 contract
questions: Why can a futures contract trade below zero when physical storage is constrained?
How should contract expiry, liquidity, margin and roll mechanics be separated from spot fundamentals?
What risk controls would a portfolio or product need before exposing users to futures data?
cases.source_note: US Energy Information Administration explains the negative close, storage constraints, low liquidity and approaching contract expiration.
cases.caveat: A single futures settlement is not a stock price, spot price, or investable strategy result.
